from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, displayed derived coefficient-adjunction and inverse-limit calculation: auxiliary localization mapping-space foundation; ordinary two-sided bar comparison (Dwyer–Kan Proposition 9.5), used in proof 10.6 before taking the simplicial-degree diagonal.

title: Ordinary two-sided categorical bar and Grothendieck nerve comparison
statement:
Use small ordinary categories, their nerves $NA$ (strings of composable arrows), and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]; use the simplex category $\Delta$ and simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Fix a small category $C$, functors $F:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ and $G:C\to\mathrm{Cat}$, and small values in a fixed larger universe. Let $E(C,F,G)$ have objects $(a,c,b)$ with $a\in F(c)$, $b\in G(c)$ and morphisms $(a,c,b)\to(a',c',b')$ given by $h:c\to c'$, $u:a\to F(h)a'$, $v:G(h)b\to b'$. Composition with $(h',u',v')$ is $(h'h,F(h)(u')u,v'G(h')(v))$, and identities are identities in the three components.

Define the trisimplicial set
$$T(C,F,G)_{i,k,j}=\coprod_{c_0\xrightarrow{h_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_k}c_k}N_iF(c_k)\times N_jG(c_0).$$
The $i,j$ directions are the ordinary nerve operators. In the $k$ direction an interior face composes adjacent base arrows, $d_0$ deletes $c_0$ and applies $G(h_1)$ to its nerve factor, $d_k$ deletes $c_k$ and applies $F(h_k)$ to its nerve factor; degeneracies repeat a base vertex with an identity arrow. Write $B(C,F,G)_r=T(C,F,G)_{r,r,r}$, with all three operators applied together. There is a finite zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences between $B(C,F,G)$ and $NE(C,F,G)$, of a fixed shape and natural in all these data. Precisely, the intermediate simplicial sets and every arrow of the zigzag are functorial under a functor $H:C'\to C$ and natural transformations $\alpha:F'\Rightarrow F H^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\beta:G'\Rightarrow GH$; their maps commute with every zigzag arrow, preserve identities and composition in $(H,\alpha,\beta)$, and at the two ends are the map of $B$ applying $H$ to the base chain and $\alpha,\beta$ to the endpoint nerve factors and the nerve of the functor $E(C',F',G')\to E(C,F,G)$ applying $(\alpha,H,\beta)$ to the three components. No equivalence hypothesis on $H,\alpha,\beta$ is needed for this naturality.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Definition 9.1, Proposition 9.5 and its proof 9.7–9.10, printed pp.31–33 (PDF pp.15–17). The chain c_0→…→c_k is the source chain W_k→…→W_0 with indices reversed. The comparison is the natural zigzag constructed there; no Stacks tag states this homotopy-theoretic comparison.

proof.text: Put $A=E(C,F,*)$, where $*$ is the terminal category, and let $P:A\to C$ forget the $F$ component. Thus objects of $A$ are $(c,a)$ and an arrow $(c,a)\to(c',a')$ is $(h,u)$ with $u:a\to F(h)a'$. For each $c$ form $D(c)=(c\downarrow P)$: objects are $(x,t:c\to Px)$ and an arrow to $(x',t')$ is $v:x\to x'$ with $P(v)t=t'$. Precomposition in $t$ makes $D:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a strict functor. Define $R_c:D(c)\to F(c)$ by $R_c((d,a),t)=F(t)a$. If $v=(h,u)$ and $ht=t'$, put $R_c(v)=F(t)u$; its target is $F(t)F(h)a'=F(t')a'$. The equalities for identities and composites follow from those of $F$. Precomposition gives $R_cD(s)=F(s)R_{c'}$ for $s:c\to c'$, so $R:D\Rightarrow F$ is strictly natural. The functor $J_c:F(c)\to D(c)$ takes $a$ to $((c,a),1_c)$. Then $R_cJ_c=1$, and the arrows $(t,1):J_cR_c(x,t)\to(x,t)$ give a natural transformation $J_cR_c\Rightarrow1$. Consequently [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] makes every $NR_c$ a weak homotopy equivalence. The choices $J_c$ need not be natural in $c$; only $R$ is used to define the comparison map.

source.place: Definition 9.1 and proof 9.10, first assertion: explicit comma-fiber retraction.

proof.text: Let $M=\operatorname{diag}T(C,D,G)$. The natural transformation $R$ gives a simplicial map $r:M\to B(C,F,G)$. Here the formulas defining $T$ apply to the new strict functor $D$ without any change. A coproduct of weak homotopy equivalences over a fixed small set is a weak homotopy equivalence: the realization quotient retains the summand index, so realization is the disjoint union, and its components and based homotopy groups are computed in the corresponding summand. For fixed $k,j$, the map $T(C,D,G)_{\bullet,k,j}\to T(C,F,G)_{\bullet,k,j}$ is a coproduct of copies of the weak equivalences $NR_{c_k}$, indexed by the base chains and the set $N_jG(c_0)$. Thus it is a weak equivalence in the first direction. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] first in $(i,k)$ for each fixed $j$, and then in $(i=k,j)$. The resulting diagonal map is exactly $r$, hence $r$ is a weak equivalence. Empty coproducts cause no exception.

source.place: Proof 9.10, left comparison of Lemma 9.7; factorwise diagonal argument expanded without using Corollary 9.6 circularly.

proof.text:
Here is the terminal-slice calculation needed for the other comparison. Fix $c\in C$, let $I_c=C/c$ have objects $t:d\to c$, and let $G_c:I_c\to\mathrm{Cat}$ send $(d,t)$ to $G(d)$. There is an augmentation
$$\epsilon_c:\mathrm{BK}_{I_c}(NG_c)\longrightarrow NG(c)$$
that sends a simplex consisting of a chain $(d_0,t_0)\to\cdots\to(d_q,t_q)$ and $z\in N_qG(d_0)$ to $N_qG(t_0)z$. It commutes with the first face because $t_1h_1=t_0$, and with every other face or degeneracy by functoriality. To prove it is a weak equivalence, apply [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison] to get the natural weak equivalence $\tau:\mathrm{BK}_{I_c}(NG_c)\to N\operatorname{Th}_{I_c}G_c$. Define $L:\operatorname{Th}_{I_c}G_c\to G(c)$ by $L((d,t),z)=G(t)z$ and $L(h,v)=G(t')v$, where $t'h=t$. The inclusion $J(z)=((c,1_c),z)$ has $LJ=1$, and the arrows $(t,1):((d,t),z)\to JL((d,t),z)$ form a natural transformation $1\Rightarrow JL$. Thus $NL$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence]. Apply naturality of $\tau$ under the unique functor $I_c\to[0]$ and the natural transformation $G_c\Rightarrow\operatorname{const}G(c)$ with components $G(t)$: it says $NL\,\tau=\tau_0\epsilon_c$. The point comparison $\tau_0:NG(c)\to NG(c)$ is a weak equivalence by the same Thomason statement, whether or not it is identified with the identity. By the weak-equivalence definition quoted in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], composition and two-of-three follow by composing bijections and homotopy-group isomorphisms and cancelling them; hence $\epsilon_c$ is a weak equivalence. This uses the actual augmentation formula, rather than choosing a homotopy inverse of a comparison.

source.place: Proof 9.10, terminal overcategory homotopy-colimit augmentation, derived using the existing one-sided Thomason theorem.

proof.text:
Take the partial diagonal $S_{i,q}=T(C,D,G)_{i,q,q}$. An $i$-simplex in $D(c_q)$ is uniquely a chain $x_0\xrightarrow{v_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{v_i}x_i$ in $A$ together with $t:c_q\to Px_0$; its other comma arrows are $P(v_a\cdots v_1)t$. Hence, for each fixed $i$, there is an isomorphism of $q$-simplicial sets
$$S_{i,\bullet}=\coprod_{x_0\to\cdots\to x_i\text{ in }A}\mathrm{BK}_{C/Px_0}(NG_{Px_0}).$$
A summand simplex records $c_0\to\cdots\to c_q\xrightarrow{t}Px_0$ and $z\in N_qG(c_0)$; equivalently it is the chain in $C/Px_0$ whose arrows to $Px_0$ are the corresponding composites. Endpoint faces in the original $k$ direction respectively apply $G$ to the first arrow and precompose the last comma arrow, exactly as in this simplicial replacement; nerve operators in $G$ act on $z$. Let
$$U_{i,j}=\coprod_{x_0\to\cdots\to x_i\text{ in }A}N_jG(Px_0).$$
The $i$ first face applies $G(Pv_1)$, other $i$ faces compose or delete the chain, and $i$ degeneracies insert identities; $j$ operators are nerve operators. Thus $U$ is bisimplicial and $\operatorname{diag}U=\mathrm{BK}_A(N(GP))$ with the convention of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus]. On the displayed summand define $e:S_{i,q}\to U_{i,q}$ by $z\mapsto G(t h_q\cdots h_1)z$.

source.place: Proof 9.10, regrouping the partial diagonal by chains in F tensor_C *, with indices reversed from the printed source.

proof.text:
Check the remaining operators of $e$. Deleting $x_0$ in a comma-category nerve chain replaces its last comma arrow $t:c_q\to Px_0$ by $P(v_1)t:c_q\to Px_1$. Applying $e$ therefore gives $G(Pv_1)G(t h_q\cdots h_1)z$, precisely the first $i$ face of $U$ after $e$. The other $i$ faces only compose or delete arrows after $x_0$ and leave the evaluated element unchanged; degeneracies insert identities. In the $q$ direction the augmentation commutes with all operators by the formula in Step 3. Thus $e:S\to U$ is a bisimplicial map. For every $i$, Step 4 identifies $e_{i,\bullet}$ with the coproduct, over all $A$-chains of length $i$, of the weak equivalences $\epsilon_{Px_0}$ from Step 3. The disjoint-union argument in Step 2 makes it a weak equivalence, including when there are no such chains. By [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence], its diagonal
$$e:M\longrightarrow\mathrm{BK}_A(N(GP))$$
is a weak equivalence; the domain is $M$ since the diagonal of $S$ has entries $T(C,D,G)_{q,q,q}$.

source.place: Proof 9.10, right comparison of Lemma 9.7; first-face compatibility and diagonal explicitly verified.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison] once more to the small category $A$ and diagram $GP:A\to\mathrm{Cat}$. It gives a natural weak equivalence
$$\mathrm{BK}_A(N(GP))\longrightarrow N\operatorname{Th}_A(GP).$$
The category on the right is canonically isomorphic to $E(C,F,G)$: its object $((c,a),b)$ is $(a,c,b)$; an arrow is $(h,u)$ in $A$ and $v:G(h)b\to b'$, exactly the three components of the stated arrow in $E$. Its composition is $(h'h,F(h)(u')u,v'G(h')(v))$, so this correspondence preserves composition and identities, with the inverse given by the same regrouping. Its nerve is an isomorphism, so its realization is an isomorphism and it is a weak equivalence by the definition quoted in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Combining this map with Steps 2 and 5 gives the fixed three-arrow zigzag
$$B(C,F,G)\xleftarrow{\ r\ }M\xrightarrow{\ e\ }\mathrm{BK}_A(N(GP))\longrightarrow NE(C,F,G).$$
All its arrows are weak homotopy equivalences. This proves the comparison without introducing another lemma that restates it.

source.place: Proof 9.9: E is the iterated one-sided Grothendieck construction; the final one-sided comparison is supplied by the existing Thomason node.

proof.text:
Verify strict naturality of the whole zigzag. For data $(H,\alpha,\beta)$ as in the statement, let $\widehat H:A'\to A$ send $(c',a')$ to $(Hc',\alpha_{c'}a')$ and use $(Hh',\alpha_{c'}u')$ on arrows; naturality of $\alpha$ identifies the target with $F(Hh')\alpha_{d'}a''$. Then $P\widehat H=HP'$ strictly. There is a functor $D'(c')\to D(Hc')$, $(x',t')\mapsto(\widehat Hx',Ht')$. It commutes with precomposition, and
$$R_{Hc'}(\widehat Hx',Ht')=\alpha_{c'}R'_{c'}(x',t')$$
by naturality of $\alpha$. Along with $\beta$, it defines the map $M'\to M$ by applying $H$ to base arrows, $\widehat H$ to comma chains, and $\beta$ to the $G$ factor. This equality proves commutation with $r$. For $e$, put $s=t'h'_q\cdots h'_1:c'_0\to P'x'_0$ in a simplex of Step 4. The two resulting evaluated elements are equal by
$$\beta_{P'x'_0}G'(s)=G(Hs)\beta_{c'_0}.$$
Their base chain is the image under $\widehat H$, so this proves commutation with $e$ on every simplex. Finally $\beta P'$ gives $G'P'\Rightarrow GP\widehat H$; the naturality under reindexing and diagram transformations of [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison] proves commutation with the last arrow. The regrouping $\operatorname{Th}_A(GP)\cong E(C,F,G)$ sends its induced functor to exactly $(\alpha,H,\beta)$ on objects and the specified three components on arrows. At the other end $r$ has target the bar map applying $H,\alpha,\beta$, by its definition. The identity data give identity functors and maps at every stage, and composing data composes their action on every component of these tuples; thus the maps preserve identities and composition strictly. All categories, comma categories, products and coproducts remain small in the fixed larger universe. If $C$ is empty all four simplicial sets are empty. If either endpoint fiber is empty the corresponding summands vanish; if both endpoint functors are terminal, the construction specializes to a natural zigzag from $NC$ to itself. No nonemptiness or equivalence hypothesis was used.

source.place: Definition 9.1 naturality and proof 9.7–9.10; explicit functoriality under simultaneous base and endpoint changes.

proof_origin.place: Dwyer–Kan Proposition 9.5, Lemma 9.7 and proofs 9.9–9.10, printed pp.31–33 (PDF pp.15–17), read online.
